newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds unchanged, spreads firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds unchanged, spreads firm.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds were unchanged in quiet midday trading in line with U.S. Treasuries with spreads seen firm across the board, dealers said.
"Spreads are tight and because of this there's very little incentive to buy and sell bonds in the Street...it's just slim pickins'," one high-grade trader said.
Other traders saw a little bit more activity on the bid side of the market but agreed that the recent drought of new corporate debt issues has dampened secondary trade.

"There's a lack of new issues...a couple may come to market but nothing's going to loosen up secondary spreads," another trader said. "We've seen a little bit more action on the bid side of the market but there's just no trading volume to speak of."
Meanwhile, corporate debt issuers are expected to tap the primary market and take advantage of a dip in U.S. Treasury yields to finance debt while rates are lower, dealers said.
Earlier, Travelers/Aetna priced $200 million in A2/A rated three-year notes to yield 25 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Dealers expect issuance may pick up as U.S. corporations rush to finance debt as speculation of a Federal Reserve Board tightening in monetary policy continues to mount.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the policy setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board, is scheduled to meet on September 24 to address U.S. monetary policy.
Meanwhile, a number of deals are lined up to come to market but no official dates have been set, dealers said.
GTE Hawaiian Telephone Co, a unit of GTE Corp, is expected to price $150 million in 10-year debentures via competitive bid, sources said.

In addition, numerous finance and bank names are circulating around the new issue arena including Wells Fargo, Signet Bank, Nationsbank, Key Bank, Australia/New Zealand Bank, and Argentaria Bank with a $250 million yankee offering, sources said.
In the private placement sector, United USN Inc is expected to set $155 million in eight-year 144A senior notes.
Also, First Nationwide Holdings is expected to price $525 million in seven-year senior subordinated 144A notes via Smith Barney.
